title_en: Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Preventing and Sanctioning False Litigation
keywords_en: private lending; divorce; bankruptcy; guarantee; labor dispute
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Guiding Opinions on Preventing and Sanctioning False Litigation

Fa Fa [2016] No. 13

Currently, false litigation in the field of civil and commercial adjudication not only seriously infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of non-parties and undermines social integrity, but also disrupts normal litigation order and impairs judicial authority and credibility, to which the people have strongly reacted. People's courts at all levels should attach great importance to this and strive to explore various effective measures to prevent and sanction false litigation.

1. False litigation generally contains the following elements: (1) the purpose is to circumvent laws, regulations, or national policies to seek illegal benefits; (2) the parties engage in malicious collusion; (3) facts are fabricated; (4) legal civil procedures are borrowed; (5) the legitimate rights and interests of the state, public interests, or non-parties are infringed upon.

2. In practice, special attention should be paid to the following circumstances: (1) the parties are in close relationships such as spouses, friends, or associated enterprises with common interests; (2) the amount in dispute claimed by the plaintiff is seriously inconsistent with his or her own economic situation; (3) the facts and reasons on which the plaintiff's claim is based are obviously unreasonable; (4) there is no substantial dispute over civil rights and interests between the parties; (5) the evidence in the case is insufficient, but the parties nevertheless voluntarily and promptly reach a mediation agreement and request the court to issue a mediation document.

3. People's courts at all levels shall post warning and publicity signs at case filing windows and courtrooms, and in the "Risk Warning for Civil Litigation in People's Courts" shall clearly inform of the legal liabilities to be borne for participating in false litigation, guiding the parties to exercise their litigation rights lawfully and conduct litigation in good faith.

4. In the trial of cases in high-incidence areas of false litigation such as private lending, divorce and property division, debt discharge through property transfer, labor disputes, company division (merger), and enterprise bankruptcy, the examination of evidence shall be strengthened. For cases where false litigation may exist, the efforts to investigate and collect evidence ex officio shall be appropriately increased.

5. If false litigation is suspected, the party shall be summoned to appear in court to be questioned regarding the facts of the case. Except for statutory reasons, witnesses shall be required to testify in court. The provisions of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law regarding parties and witnesses signing affidavits shall be fully utilized, and systems for oaths by parties and witnesses shall be explored.

6. During litigation, if one party clearly admits a fact unfavorable to itself proposed by the other party, and such admission is inconsistent with common sense, further verification shall be conducted and recognition shall be made with caution. If the facts found are inconsistent with the admitted facts, the admission shall not be confirmed.

7. The examination of mediation agreements shall be strengthened. For cases where the parties voluntarily reach a mediation agreement and request the court to issue a mediation document, the court shall, in light of the basic facts of the case, focus on examining whether the mediation agreement harms the national interest, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of non-parties. For cases of judicial confirmation of people's mediation agreements, attention shall be paid, as required by the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, to examining the authenticity of the underlying legal relationship.

8. In the process of enforcing legal documents such as notarized debt instruments and arbitration awards, mediation documents, etc., if malicious collusion or fabrication of facts between the parties may exist, substantive review shall be intensified, focusing on whether the relevant legal documents harm the national interest, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of non-parties. If such circumstances exist, an order shall be made to refuse enforcement. When necessary, judicial recommendations may be issued to the arbitration institution or notary authority.

9. The openness of trials shall be enhanced to increase the transparency of case proceedings. For persons who may have a legal interest in the outcome of the case, they may be notified ex officio to participate in the proceedings as appropriate, to prevent harm to their civil rights and interests and to prevent false litigation.

10. In the trial of cases such as third-party revocation actions, enforcement objection lawsuits by non-parties, and retrial applications by non-parties, if it is found that an effective judgment involves false litigation, correction shall be made promptly to protect the procedural and substantive rights of non-parties; at the same time, care shall be taken to prevent relevant persons from using the above legal systems to create false litigation and harm the interests of legitimate rights holders in the original lawsuit.

11. If it is ascertained that a case constitutes false litigation and the plaintiff applies to withdraw the lawsuit, the application shall not be granted, and the court shall, in accordance with Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law, dismiss the claim.

12. For participants in false litigation, the application of coercive measures against obstruction of civil proceedings, such as fines and detention, shall be appropriately increased. If false litigation infringes upon the civil rights and interests of others, the participants in the false litigation shall bear compensatory liability. If the illegal acts of false litigation are suspected of constituting crimes such as the crime of false litigation, the crime of fraud, or the crime of contract fraud, the civil adjudication department shall transfer the relevant leads and case materials to the investigative authorities in accordance with the law.

13. The establishment of a list system for dishonest persons in false litigation shall be explored. Participants in false litigation shall be included in the list of dishonest persons, and efforts shall be gradually made to connect with existing relevant information platforms and the social credit system to increase the intensity of sanctions.

14. If personnel of people's courts participate in false litigation, they shall be dealt with strictly in accordance with the Judges Law, the Basic Code of Ethics for Judges, the Code of Conduct for Judges, and other relevant provisions.

15. If litigation agents participate in false litigation, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law, and judicial recommendations shall be issued to the judicial administrative departments, bar associations, or industry associations.

16. If appraisal institutions or appraisers participate in false litigation, sanctions such as reprimand, an order to refund appraisal fees, and removal from the court's list of professional institutions for entrusted appraisals may be imposed on the appraisal institution or appraiser depending on the severity of the circumstances, and judicial recommendations shall be issued to the judicial administrative departments or industry associations.

17. Proactive communication and coordination with relevant departments shall be conducted to seek support and cooperation, and the establishment of a multi-departmental coordinated comprehensive governance mechanism shall be explored. False litigation illegal acts shall be deterred through various forms, such as publicly releasing typical cases of false litigation to the public.

18. People's courts at all levels shall promptly organize their officers to study and understand various economic and social policies of the central and local governments, fully anticipate the types of false litigation cases that may be reflected in the judicial field, and may also adopt various forms such as analyzing typical cases, exchanging trial expertise, and observing court hearings to improve the judicial capacity to identify false litigation.

June 20, 2016
